title: The Last Key
brief: At the last ferry departure, a booth keeper must choose whether to surrender the key that ends her shift.

formula.style_constant: Muted rust and green, tactile canvas and worn brass; restrained contrast and patient framing.

assets.descriptor: Mara wears a rust canvas jacket with a square brass clasp.
assets.voice: A low, dry voice; deliberate consonants and a short breath before each line.
assets.behavior: She steadies loose objects before answering.

assets.descriptor: Iven wears a charcoal apron with a stitched white corner.
assets.voice: A light, close voice with an even pace and soft final consonants.
assets.behavior: He keeps his hands open whenever he asks for something.

assets.descriptor: A flat brass key with one triangular notch.
A flat brass key with one triangular notch, resting flat on the table.
A narrow ferry ticket booth with a green counter and a round clock.

scenes.title: The counter at closing
scenes.dramatic_question: Will Mara give up the key when leaving means abandoning her post?
scenes.prose:
The clock ticks past closing. Iven holds out his hand. Mara braces the key in her palm.

IVEN: The last boat is waiting.

Mara covers the notch with her thumb. She lays the key on the counter.

MARA: Then let it wait.

Iven pulls his hand back. The key stays between them.
